content.comment_body: Hello! I received my new [article_no] and created a simple project to test the [product_name] Web Editor, but I am unable to access it through the web server. The sample project (Swimming pool) from the [company_name] website works fine for me. Could you advise what might be missing in my project? I've attached some images for reference. Thanks.
Are you able to call up the web server without having selected the user-defined pages?
Did you make sure to enable access to the web server under access control?

Yes, I enabled access to the web server in [product_name] [product_name], and was able to access the Swimming pool sample from the [company_name] website. But with my own project, I can't access it. Can you clarify what you mean by 'without selecting user-defined pages'?
Could you upload your [product_name] and [product_name] projects to the forum as a ZIP file?
I've attached my test project. I appreciate your assistance.

The issue is with the digital value 'STOP'. You haven’t set the 'writeable' option in its properties. Additionally, the circuit design could be improved—the web server treats the bit as a continuous signal. For example, clicking 'START' will set M1 high until you click again, behaving as a switch. This is shown in the attached video.

Did you update anything other than the writeable property for the STOP digital element? I changed it but still couldn’t access my project via the web server. Which screen recorder do you use? I could send a short video to demonstrate my issue. Is it possible to create a pushbutton, or only a switch, on the web server? Thanks.

When I accessed the user-defined page you created, it worked instantly—the START button activated the latching relay. The STOP button didn’t work until I set the 'writable' property in the [product_name] Web Editor and transferred the project to the [product_name]. However, the Web Editor doesn’t let you select between 'Button' or 'Switch' controls. I work around this by using V-bits and resetting the corresponding V-bit in [product_name]. For screen recordings, I use Snap10 Ashampoo.
This first screen capture shows the issue I’m having with my own project.

This next capture demonstrates that the sample project from the [company_name] website works properly. Something seems to be missing in my test project. What are V-bits? I’ve never used those with [product_name].

A '404' error means the requested page isn’t found on the web server. When I transferred your project to my [product_name], I got the same error. After re-uploading my own project, I had full access. It seems there’s some issue with your project. I’ll create a new one for you using V-bits.
So you tried my project, saw the same error, then recreated a similar one and it worked? Is that correct?

Question: Did you rename your project directory after saving? For example, from 'lwe1' to 'essai1'? When I do this, I get a 404 error. If I keep the directory name the same as before, I have no problems.
If the project is named 'essai1,' the error occurs, even if that’s the original name. Renaming the project back to something like 'lwe1' resolves the issue for me.
Attached is my project using V-bits.

I renamed my project to 'lwe1' and it now works, so the project name must match the folder name. It’s unusual! I’ll review your V-bit project later. Thanks for your valuable help—I’ll be able to try out more complete projects now.

After further testing, I discovered the issue: you cannot save a project named 'XYZ' inside a folder also named 'XYZ.' The [product_name] Web Editor then takes the folder name as the project name and tries to load data from the 'XYZ' folder instead of the 'XYZ' project.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered problems accessing custom projects through the web server in the [product_name] Web Editor, while sample projects worked without issue. Through troubleshooting, it became clear that correct property settings for digital elements (like ensuring 'writeable') are necessary and that naming conventions (project and folder names) impact accessibility. There was also confusion regarding UI controls (pushbutton versus switch) and the handling of bits (V-bits). These usability challenges suggest the need for clearer guidance in the software and greater flexibility in the user interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that custom web pages created with the [product_name] Web Editor can be accessed through the web server with the same ease and reliability as sample projects, including having configurable interface components like pushbuttons.
